DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 17 s. 2022 21 MAR 2022 Mr. ROMEO DELA SANTA Site Administrator Rich Court Realty and Development Inc. Dear Mr. Dela Santa: This has reference to your letter, dated 20 December 2021 , seeking legal opinion from this Department regarding the professional squatters and squatting syndicates found inside the subject properties in Sangandaan, Caloocan City. Per your letter, due to rampant use, sale, and lease of the subject properties as permanent residences and business establishments by illegal occupants without the express consent and approval of Rich Court and using spurious titles such as TCT No. 12022 and OCT No. 014, Rich Court is seeking assistance and guidance from this Department, in identifying these illegal occupants as professional squatters, if warranted. At the outset, please be informed that R.A. 7279, otherwise known as the Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992, is specific as to who are "professional squatters", viz: "SEC. 3. Definition of Terms. — For purposes of this Act: x xxx (m) "Professional squatters" refers to individuals or qroups who occupy lands without the express consent of the landowner and who have sufficient income for Ieqitimate housinq. The term shall also apply to persons who have previously been awarded homelots or housing units by the govemment but who sold, leased or transferred the same to settle illegally in the same place or in another urban area, and non-bona fide occupants and intruders of lands reserved for socialized housing. The term shall not apply to individuals or groups who simply rent land and housing from professional squatters or squattinq syndicates: x x x x" (Emphasis and underlining supplied) From the above-definition, professional squatters are individuals or groups who occupy the subject properties without the express consent of Rich Court and must have "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

sufficient income for legitimate housing. Per your letter, there is also a rampant lease of the subject properties. However, please take note that this term does not apply to individuals who simply rent land and housing from professional squatters. Only those who use and occupy the subject properties can be considered professional squatters. As to those who sell the subject properties as permanent residences and business establishments to illegal occupants without the express consent and approval of Rich Court, they are considered "Squatting syndicates" under R.A. 7279, thus: "(s) "Squatting syndicates" refers to groups of persons engaged in the business of squatter housing for profit or gain;" Relatively, the identification of these professional squatters or members of squatting syndicates lies with the LGU in cooperation with the Presidential Commission of the Urban Poor (PCUP), Philippine National Police (PNP) and accredited Urban Poor organization (UPO).I Upon identification of these professional squatters, eviction and demolition may be effected by the LGU of Caloocan City through summary eviction2 under Section 27 and judicial eviction under Section 28 (c) of RA 7279, viz: "Section 27. Action Against Professional Squatters and Squatting Syndicates. —The local govemment units, in cooperation with the Philippine National Police, the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP), and the PCUP-accredited urban poor organization in the area, shall adopt measures to identify and effectively curtail the nefarious and illegal activities of professional squatters and squatting syndicates, as herein defined. Any person or group identified as such shall be summarily evicted and their dwellings or structures demolished and shall be disqualified to avail of the benefits of the Program. A public official who tolerates or abets the commission of the abovementioned acts shall be dealt with in accordance with existing laws. x xxx In the event that those identified do not fall under the classification of professional squatters and/or squatting syndicates, their treatment depends on the LGUs validation on when the structures were constructed. If the dwelling/structures were constructed prior to the effectivity of R.A. No. 7279, the provisions under Section 28 will apply. On the other hand, if the dwellings/structures were constructed after the effectivity of R.A. No. 7279, Section 2(1.0) of its Implementing Rules and Regulations states that new squatter families whose structures were built after the effectivity of R.A. No. 7279 shall be subject of summary eviction3 1 Section 27 of RA 7279 (rephrased). 2 Implementing Rules and Regulations Governing Summary Eviction dated November 3, 1993. 3 The procedures and guidelines for summary eviction is govemed by Section 3, IRR of R.A. No. 7279, and this IRR was crafted pursuant to Section 443 of R.A. No. 7279. Page 2 of 3

Further, per your letter, certain barangay kagawads of Barangay 3, Zone I of Caloocan City are tolerating professional squatters and squatting syndicates in the subject premises. Sec. 27 of RA 7279, the law provides: "x xxx Any person or group identified as such shall be summarily evicted and their dwellings or structures demolished and shall be disqualified to avail of the benefits of the Program. A public official who tolerates or abets the commission of the abovementioned acts shall be dealt with in accordance with existinq laws." (Emphasis supplied) However, for purposes of this discussion, it is noteworthy that the photos attached by Rich Court of certain barangay kagawads inside the premises of the subject property do not necessarily mean that they are tolerating the professional squatters and squatting syndicates. Such matter is factual and legal issue which is beyond the jurisdiction of this Department. Please be informed that such issue is within the jurisdiction of the proper court tribunals. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: RLO Underse .1 NGAN tary for Local Government Page 3 of 3
